title: IAEA/NEA nuclear incident reporting systems as operating-experience memory rails
summary: IRSNI is encoded as nuclear operating-experience infrastructure: a set of incident-reporting systems that collect, analyse, maintain, and disseminate safety-related event reports from participating countries. It is not encoded as proof that lessons are public, complete, or infused into practice.

status_history.note: Added as nuclear OPEX correction-memory rail.

claims.claim: The IAEA says it administers three incident reporting systems for nuclear installations to collect, analyse, maintain, and disseminate reports from participating countries on safety-related events; reports describe events, analyse causes, and highlight corrective actions and lessons learned.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The IAEA page describes the nuclear-power-plant IRS as a jointly managed IAEA/OECD-NEA system for exchanging operational experience to improve nuclear-power-plant safety; it was established in 1980 and had 37 participating countries in 2022.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: For the cube, IRSNI is an operating-experience memory rail: it helps convert events into shareable lessons, but its existence alone does not establish public completeness, cross-border uptake, or actual design/procedure infusion.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: correction memory versus correction infusion pattern

limitations: No effectiveness or completeness audit performed.

type_payload.signal_capture_model: authorized participating countries submit nuclear-installation event reports; reports are analysed and shared through IAEA/NEA-managed systems and meetings
limitations: public access to detailed event reports is limited
reporting quality and dissemination depend on participating states and organizations
existence of a reporting rail is not evidence of lesson infusion
